candidates.source_name: IFC Project Disclosure Portal (disclosures.ifc.org)
candidates.why_relevant: IFC is contractually obliged to publish a Summary of Investment Information (SII) before Board approval for every investment, including its Ukrainian bank exposures (PrivatBank, Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine, Ukrgasbank, ProCredit). SII pages give counterparty legal name, instrument type, size, ownership, use of proceeds and E&S category — often the earliest public confirmation of a bank-level transaction, ahead of the bank's own disclosure.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic crawl of project-detail pages filtered by country=Ukraine and industry=Financial Institutions; parse SII fields; monitor for new project IDs
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball from project pages
queries_used: IFC Ukraine banking project disclosure summary investment

candidates.source_name: EBRD Project Summary Documents (PSD) search / project portal
candidates.why_relevant: EBRD PSDs are the mandatory pre-signing factual summary of each project. Filterable by country=Ukraine, sector=Financial Institutions, project type (Investment vs Technical Cooperation), and status. This is the canonical register of EBRD equity stakes, risk-sharing facilities, guarantees and trade-finance lines to Ukrainian banks, plus TC projects with the NBU on financial-sector strategy and payments.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the projects listing with Ukraine + Financial Institutions filters; the underlying listing is JS-driven so use a headless browser or the per-project /projects/psd/<id>.html and /projects/tcpsd/<id>.html patterns
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + direct fetch of the EBRD projects portal
queries_used: EBRD Ukraine bank project summary document equity investment
EBRD project summary documents search Ukraine financial institutions psd bank

candidates.source_name: EBRD news and press releases — Ukraine financial institutions
candidates.why_relevant: EBRD announces Ukrainian bank transactions (guarantee programmes with PrivatBank, Ukrgasbank, Raiffeisen, OTP, ProCredit, Kredobank; equity funds such as Dragon Capital Rebuild Ukraine Fund) with headline volumes, EU first-loss structure and named counterparties. Faster and more candid than issuer IR during wartime; also carries annual Ukraine deployment totals (EUR 2.9bn in 2025, EUR 10.5bn cumulative wartime).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: RSS/news-listing scrape filtered on 'Ukraine' + bank names; link out to the PSD referenced in each release
queries_used: EBRD Ukraine bank project summary document equity investment

candidates.source_name: IMF Ukraine country page and Staff Country Reports (EFF reviews, Article IV)
candidates.why_relevant: IMF EFF review staff reports carry the most systematic public dataset on Ukrainian banking: financial soundness indicators tables, capital/liquidity ratios, NPLs, net interest margin, sovereign exposure share of bank assets, bank-resolution and state-bank-privatisation structural benchmarks. Programme conditionality doubles as a forward calendar of banking-sector reform.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor imf.org/en/Publications/CR for Ukraine reports and the country page press releases; PDF text extraction of the FSI and financial-sector annex tables per review
queries_used: IMF Ukraine EFF review staff report banking sector financial soundness indicators

candidates.source_name: IMF eLibrary (Ukraine staff country reports, structured)
candidates.why_relevant: Machine-friendlier XML/HTML rendering of the same IMF Ukraine staff reports, easier to parse than PDF for FSI tables and Memorandum of Economic and Financial Policies annexes.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Article-level fetch of Ukraine CR volumes; store references only, avoid bulk redistribution
queries_used: IMF Ukraine EFF review staff report banking sector financial soundness indicators

candidates.source_name: NBU publication of the Memorandum on Economic and Financial Policies (Ukrainian translation)
candidates.why_relevant: The NBU and MoF publish Ukrainian translations of the Letter of Intent / Memorandum про економічну та фінансову політику agreed with the IMF. These carry banking-sector commitments (state bank strategy, NPL resolution, DGF/Фонд гарантування вкладів reform) in the local terminology used by Ukrainian regulators and media — essential for local-language matching.
candidates.source_subtype: central bank republication of IMF programme document
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Watch bank.gov.ua and mof.gov.ua IMF sections for new MEFP/LoI PDFs after each EFF review
queries_used: Світовий банк Україна проєкт фінансовий сектор документи МВФ меморандум банківський сектор
local_language_terms_used: Меморандум про економічну та фінансову політику

candidates.source_name: Ministry of Finance of Ukraine — IFI cooperation pages (ЄБРР / Світовий банк / МВФ / ЄІБ)
candidates.why_relevant: The MoF maintains per-IFI landing pages with cumulative portfolio figures, the list of active sovereign and sovereign-guaranteed projects, and links to project documents. It is the authoritative Ukrainian-side roster of which IFI money is in the system and under what agreement, and it supplies the Ukrainian official names of the institutions (ЄБРР, МФК, ЄІБ, БАГІ, МБРР).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled scrape of /uk/ebrr, /uk/svitovij-bank, /uk/mvf, /uk/yevropejskij-investicijnij-bank and their EN mirrors; diff against previous snapshot
queries_used: ЄБРР інвестиція в український банк проєкт документ резюме
Світовий банк Україна проєкт фінансовий сектор документи

candidates.source_name: World Bank Projects & Operations portal — Ukraine financial sector
candidates.why_relevant: Project pages carry Program Documents, Implementation Status Reports and ICRs for Ukraine financial-sector DPLs and jobs/private-sector operations. These documents describe deposit-guarantee-fund reform, bank resolution, state bank governance and credit-infrastructure conditions with explicit prior actions and results indicators.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Query the World Bank Projects API by country=Ukraine and sector=Finance; pull attached documents via the Documents & Reports API
queries_used: World Bank Ukraine projects financial sector development policy loan documents projects.worldbank.org

candidates.source_name: World Bank Documents & Reports (documents.worldbank.org)
candidates.why_relevant: Full-text archive of World Bank analytical work on Ukrainian banking and payments — sector notes, corporate governance surveys of the banking sector, financial inclusion diagnostics — retrievable back to the 1990s and covering periods where issuer disclosure is thin.
candidates.legal_status: public, CC-BY for most WB content
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Documents & Reports API (wds) with country=Ukraine, topic=Finance and Financial Sector Development; download PDFs
queries_used: IFC Ukraine banking project disclosure summary investment

candidates.source_name: World Bank Group donor financing mechanisms for Ukraine (ADVANCE, SURE, F.O.R.T.I.S. trust funds)
candidates.why_relevant: Explains the trust-fund and guarantee plumbing (ADVANCE Ukraine TF, SURE TF, F.O.R.T.I.S. FIF) that underwrites IFC/MIGA/IBRD risk in Ukrainian banks. Needed to interpret why a given bank transaction was possible and who bears first loss.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic page snapshot + diff; follow linked trust-fund annual reports
queries_used: World Bank Ukraine projects financial sector development policy loan documents

candidates.source_name: MIGA — Ukraine response and guarantee project briefs
candidates.why_relevant: MIGA issues political-risk guarantees directly to banks operating in Ukraine — notably cover on mandatory reserves held at the NBU against expropriation risk for ProCredit Bank Ukraine and peers, and the DFC-MIGA PRI framework for the US-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund. Project briefs name the guarantee holder, the bank, the amount and the covered risk, which is a direct read on foreign parent-bank capital commitment to Ukraine.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl miga.org projects listing filtered by host country Ukraine plus the press-release feed
queries_used: MIGA guarantee Ukraine bank political risk insurance project brief

candidates.source_name: EIB press releases and project list — Ukraine
candidates.why_relevant: EIB and EIF disclose EU4Business Guarantee Facility agreements with named Ukrainian banks (PrivatBank, Ukreximbank, Ukrgasbank, ProCredit, plus seven-bank tranches), including guarantee size and expected mobilised lending. EIB also runs a public project register with pre-approval publication requirements.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape eib.org press listing filtered on Ukraine; cross-reference the EIB financed-projects register for the matching operation entry
queries_used: EIB Ukraine financing projects list bank SME European Investment Bank disclosure

candidates.source_name: U.S. DFC press releases and Ukraine transactions
candidates.why_relevant: DFC discloses equity and debt commitments touching Ukrainian financial services — Horizon Capital Growth Fund IV, the US-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund (URIF) seeded at USD 75m, and the DFC-MIGA political-risk-insurance framework. DFC is also statutorily required to post project-level information ahead of board consideration.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape the press-release index filtered on Ukraine; separately monitor the DFC active-projects data export for Ukraine rows
queries_used: DFC Development Finance Corporation Ukraine bank investment project disclosure Horizon Capital

candidates.source_name: Early Warning System (ewsdata.rightsindevelopment.org) — IFI project aggregator
candidates.why_relevant: Civil-society mirror that scrapes and archives IFC, EBRD, EIB, WB and ADB project disclosures into a stable, uniformly structured record. Extremely useful because IFI portals silently revise or retire pages; EWS preserves the original disclosure text and dates, e.g. Ukrgasbank Support (IFC-41132) with its debt-to-equity conversion option, and RSF PrivatBank (IFC-50956).
candidates.source_subtype: NGO aggregator / archive of IFI disclosures
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl country=Ukraine project listings; treat as corroboration/archive layer, always resolve back to the originating IFI page
queries_used: IFC Ukraine banking project disclosure summary investment

candidates.source_name: Ukraine Donor Coordination Platform
candidates.why_relevant: G7-established coordination body whose members include the WB, EBRD, EIB, IMF and IFC. Its private-sector workstream, together with the KSE Institute, publishes a compendium of IFI/DFI financing and de-risking instruments available for Ukraine across 25 countries — a single map of who offers what to Ukrainian banks, and a pointer to institutions outside the obvious five.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch the private-sector support page and download successive compendium editions; use it as an actor-map seed for snowballing
queries_used: Ukraine Donor Platform openaid Ukraine donor projects database IFI financial sector

candidates.source_name: OpenAid Ukraine (openaid.gov.ua) — aid transparency portal
candidates.why_relevant: Ukrainian government portal intended to consolidate all IFI- and donor-supported development projects in Ukraine into one searchable register with Ukrainian project titles and implementing agencies — the local-language crosswalk between an EBRD/IFC project code and how the project is named in Ukrainian official and press usage.
candidates.access_status: unverified — plain HTTP, currency of data not confirmed
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Test for a project-listing/API endpoint; if only HTML, crawl the project register and store Ukrainian titles for entity matching. Verify freshness before relying on it
queries_used: Ukraine Donor Platform openaid Ukraine donor projects database IFI financial sector

candidates.source_name: EBRD-Ukraine Stabilisation and Sustainable Growth Multi-Donor Account (MDA)
candidates.why_relevant: The MDA is the donor vehicle behind much EBRD technical assistance, first-loss guarantees and concessional funding in Ukraine, including financial-sector policy work. Its annual reports and independent evaluations state which instruments were actually deployed versus merely available, giving a candid read on donor appetite for bank risk.
candidates.source_subtype: IFI donor fund reporting / independent evaluation
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download annual MDA reports and the EvD evaluation PDFs; watch the EBRD evaluation publications feed
queries_used: EBRD Ukraine Stabilisation and Sustainable Growth Multi-Donor Account annual report bank guarantees

candidates.source_name: EU4Business–EBRD Credit Line Ukraine programme site
candidates.why_relevant: Operational programme site for EBRD/EU credit lines routed through Ukrainian partner banks. Publishes the list of participating banks, programme documents (e.g. the Financial Inclusion Recovery Programme under the Ukraine Investment Framework) and eligibility terms in Ukrainian — the bank-level distribution layer that the EBRD PSD only names in the abstract.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape the partner-bank list and the wp-content document directory; diff the bank roster over time as a proxy for which banks retain IFI eligibility
queries_used: EBRD project summary documents search Ukraine financial institutions psd bank

candidates.source_name: IFC Ukraine country page
candidates.why_relevant: Portfolio-level framing for IFC's Ukraine engagement: committed volumes, the Economic Resilience Action (ERA) programme under which most bank risk-sharing facilities sit, and links to advisory work on credit reporting and financial inclusion that touches payments infrastructure.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Page snapshot + diff; follow through to disclosures.ifc.org for transaction detail
queries_used: IFC Ukraine banking project disclosure summary investment

candidates.source_name: Ukrainian partner-bank pages describing IFI programmes (e.g. Ukreximbank EBRD programme page)
candidates.why_relevant: Ukrainian banks publish their own Ukrainian-language descriptions of IFI facilities (ЄБРР, ЄІБ, МФК, Світовий банк lines) including limits, tenors and eligible borrowers. This is the mirror image of the IFI disclosure and reveals terms and local naming the IFI page omits; Ukreximbank also hosts archived World Bank project documents in Ukrainian.
candidates.source_subtype: issuer republication of IFI programme terms
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Maintain a list of Ukrainian partner banks (Ukreximbank, PrivatBank, Ukrgasbank, Oschadbank, Raiffeisen, OTP, ProCredit, Kredobank) and crawl their 'МФО / міжнародні програми' sections
queries_used: ЄБРР інвестиція в український банк проєкт документ резюме
Світовий банк Україна проєкт фінансовий сектор документи

candidates.source_name: Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine — IFI co-investment platform announcements
candidates.why_relevant: The government announces the annual coordination of cooperation directions with the EBRD and European development finance institutions under the co-investment platform (Платформа співінвестування), signalling upcoming IFI activity in the financial sector before project disclosure appears.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword monitoring of the kmu.gov.ua news feed for ЄБРР / МФК / ЄІБ / банківський сектор

negative_findings.description: No IFI project disclosure source was found that is specifically about Ukrainian PAYMENTS infrastructure (acquiring, card schemes, instant payments, POS) as opposed to bank lending. IFC advisory on credit reporting and EBRD TC with the NBU on financial-sector strategy are the closest, and both are credit/regulatory rather than payments-market disclosure.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches across IFC, EBRD, EIB and WB surfaced overwhelmingly SME-lending, guarantee and risk-sharing facilities; payments appears only incidentally inside broader financial-sector programmes.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For a payments-sector intelligence workstream, IFI disclosure will under-serve the payments half of the cell and must be complemented by NBU and scheme-level sources handled by other cells.

negative_findings.description: No Ukrainian-language mirror of IFI project-level disclosure databases was found. EBRD PSDs, IFC SIIs, MIGA project briefs and World Bank project documents for Ukraine bank transactions appear in English only; Ukrainian-language coverage comes from government republication (MoF, NBU MEFP translations), partner-bank pages and media, not from the IFIs' own registers.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ukrainian queries returned MoF/NBU/KMU pages, bank programme pages, Wikipedia and press (ZN.ua, Forbes.ua, Ekonomichna Pravda) rather than any uk-language IFI project register.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Local-language monitoring of this cell must target the Ukrainian intermediaries, not the IFIs; entity resolution needs a maintained ЄБРР/МФК/ЄІБ/БАГІ/МБРР alias table.

negative_findings.description: The EBRD project search interface applies filters client-side rather than through URL query parameters, so there is no stable deep-link for 'Ukraine + Financial Institutions + last 12 months'.
negative_findings.result_summary: Direct fetch of the EBRD projects portal showed a filter UI (country, sector, status, document type, date range) but 'dynamic filtering through the interface rather than URL parameters'.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated EBRD collection needs a headless browser or an undocumented backing JSON endpoint; naive HTTP scraping will silently return unfiltered or empty results.

negative_findings.description: openaid.gov.ua was found as the Ukrainian aid-transparency register but its current data coverage and update cadence were not established, and it was reached over plain HTTP.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only an 'About' page surfaced; described in secondary sources as a promised portal covering all IFI/donor-supported projects.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: It could be either the best Ukrainian-language crosswalk for IFI project names or an abandoned portal; must be verified before being relied on.

negative_findings.description: The cell brief anticipates 'financial covenants' in IFI disclosure. No public IFI document was found that reproduces bank-level financial covenants (capital, NPL, liquidity triggers) for a Ukrainian bank borrower.
negative_findings.result_summary: PSDs/SIIs disclose instrument type, size, use of proceeds, ownership and E&S category, but covenant schedules sit in unpublished loan agreements. IMF programme documents give system-wide prudential benchmarks, not counterparty covenants.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents over-promising covenant-level intelligence from this cell; the realistic ceiling is transaction structure plus system-level prudential conditionality.

coverage_gaps.description: Bilateral European DFIs that co-invest alongside the majors in Ukrainian financial services were identified as co-investors (Proparco, Swedfund, Finnfund, IFU, and by extension KfW/DEG, FMO, BGK) but their own disclosure registers were not scouted.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a follow-up pass over Proparco, FMO, DEG/KfW, Swedfund, Finnfund, IFU and BGK project databases filtered on Ukraine + financial sector.

coverage_gaps.description: IFI independent accountability and evaluation arms (IFC CAO, EBRD IPAM and EvD, World Bank Inspection Panel, IEG) were not systematically scouted. These publish the most candid assessments of financial-intermediary lending.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout CAO, IPAM, Inspection Panel and IEG case registers for Ukraine financial-intermediary cases and evaluations.

coverage_gaps.description: API/bulk-download endpoints were not confirmed for IFC disclosures, EBRD projects, MIGA or EIB. Only the World Bank is known to expose documented public APIs.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Technical probe for JSON endpoints, IATI publications and open-data exports per institution; record robots.txt and rate limits before scheduling collection.

coverage_gaps.description: IFI annual reports and Ukraine country strategies (EBRD Country Strategy for Ukraine, IFC country strategy, World Bank CPF) were not individually scouted, and their Ukrainian-language summaries — which the cell rationale assumes exist — were not located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout the EBRD Ukraine Country Strategy, WB Country Partnership Framework and their uk-language summaries; confirm whether Ukrainian versions are published at all.

coverage_gaps.description: IFI shareholding/equity stakes in Ukrainian banks specifically (as opposed to lending and guarantees) were only partially evidenced — the clearest case found was IFC's Ukrgasbank loan with an option to convert into up to 20 percent equity.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Targeted search per state bank (Ukrgasbank, Oschadbank, PrivatBank, Sense Bank) for IFI equity or convertible instruments, and cross-check against NBU ownership-structure disclosures.

brief: IFI and donor disclosure on Ukrainian banks is a dense, high-credibility and largely English-language layer built on four mandatory registers — IFC's disclosure portal, EBRD's Project Summary Documents, World Bank Projects & Documents, and MIGA's guarantee briefs — supplemented by EIB/EIF and US DFC press disclosure and by IMF EFF review staff reports, which carry the only systematic public banking-sector soundness indicators for Ukraine. In practice these sources reliably yield counterparty identity, instrument type, size, donor first-loss structure and system-level prudential conditionality, but not bank-level financial covenants, which remain in unpublished loan agreements. Ukrainian-language access to this material runs through intermediaries rather than the IFIs themselves: the Ministry of Finance IFI pages, NBU-published MEFP translations, EU4Business-EBRD programme sites and partner banks' own МФО pages. The main collection risks are the EBRD portal's client-side filtering (no stable deep-links), unconfirmed API availability across most institutions, and a genuine thinness on payments as distinct from bank lending.
